title: CatBoost vs XGBoost for next-day Delhi PM2.5 (isolated, retrospective experiment)

data.primary_why: production data plus OpenCity gap-fill: gives hourly day-part inputs for the 2024-25 winter, so V2 / Hybrid can be compared
data.secondary_why: exactly the data the deployed models were trained on (sensitivity check, first test only)

features.hybrid: V2 when all 7 day-part inputs are finite, else V1 (core/hybrid.py, unchanged)
features.note: CatBoost gets the same feature lists. No categorical features are declared, no feature is added or removed.

target: log1p(PM2.5 tomorrow) - log1p(PM2.5 today); prediction = expm1(log1p(today) + model output)
training_rows: forecast origins whose TARGET date is before the window start; weather = observed (ERA5 archive) weather of the target day, as in the production recipe
validation_split: last 60 training rows (chronological) are the early-stopping set for every model, XGBoost and CatBoost alike
missing_values: no imputation anywhere; day-part NaN stay NaN (both libraries handle NaN natively)

tuning.why_cutoff: the first scored winter starts 2022-10-15; tuning rows are strictly earlier, so no test period is ever seen during tuning
tuning.method: blocked forward-chaining cross-validation (sklearn TimeSeriesSplit, 6 folds, never shuffled), features = v1 25, weather = observed (the dev years have no forecast archive and no hourly day-parts)
tuning.baseline_why: mirrors the XGBoost recipe (800 trees max, lr 0.03, depth 4) with CatBoost's own default regularisation
tuning.tuned_config: the grid member with the lowest pooled out-of-fold MAE (ties within 0.1 percent go to the baseline-like, shallower, slower one)
tuning.xgboost_reference: production XGBoost recipe scored with the same folds, for comparison only (never tuned)

test.frozen_fit: one fit per window on rows with target before the window start; no refit, no early stopping on test days

T1_primary.weather: tomorrow's weather := today's observed weather (leak-free persistence of weather)
T1_primary.why: same regime as the existing back-test PRIMARY; contains no future observed weather

T2_live_like.weather: archived 24 h-ahead forecast of tomorrow's weather (Open-Meteo Previous Runs)
T2_live_like.why: the live Lambda receives a forecast; archive exists from 2024-01-20 only

T3_all_season.why: covers all four IMD seasons; fit is up to 21 months old by the end

test.never_used: tomorrow's OBSERVED weather as a test input; anything after 2026-10-07; winter 2026-27

decision_rule.primary_comparison: tuned CatBoost Hybrid vs XGBoost Hybrid, T1, primary data, seed 42
recommend_further_testing_only_if_all: pooled MAE at least 2 percent lower than XGBoost Hybrid
95 percent interval of the MAE difference entirely below zero for BOTH 7- and 14-day blocks
no single winter more than 2 percent worse
exact-category accuracy not lower by more than 2 percentage points
tuned CatBoost pooled out-of-fold MAE on the development folds not worse than XGBoost's (no benefit that exists only on already-examined winters)
decision_rule.otherwise: no evidence of improvement; keep XGBoost; CatBoost stays a documented reference only
decision_rule.multiplicity: one primary comparison; every other comparison in the report is descriptive
decision_rule.never: promote to production, change the default, retrain stored models, commit, push or deploy
